subject: Zenovia pilot — recommended model slate & action items
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@zenovia.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom@zenovia.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T15:00:00Z
Subject: Zenovia pilot — recommended model slate & action items

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation and helpful context on expected request shape (short customer messages + 1–2 context turns), SLOs (~< 350ms p95 for interactive) and initial throughput targets (peak ~60 rps). Per our call I put together a concise recommended slate of model variants for the pilot, with clear rationale and next steps so we can lock the PoC config this week. See the attached benchmark summary and prompt pack.

Recommended model slate (pilot):
- Option A — Redwood-mix-7B-quant (4-bit): Primary candidate for fastest time-to-value. Tradeoffs: lowest cost and lowest latency (estimated p95 ~120–180ms on 8xA100 shared pool), slightly lower open-domain factuality vs larger models but performs well on short-context customer Q&A.
- Option B — RedServe-13B-opt (int8 + kernel tuning): Balanced option — good cost/quality sweet spot. Estimated p95 ~220–300ms; noticeably better on nuanced disambiguation and fewer hallucinations in our evals.
- Option C — OpenLlama-65B-amp (sharded, int8): Highest quality for edge cases (legal/tech support language) but highest cost and latency (p95 ~450–600ms on dedicated 8xA100). Suggested only for fallback or selective routing on high-risk queries.

Benchmarks & evidence: attached PDF contains latency/cost curves, per-dataset QA accuracy, hallucination counts, and token-cost estimates (per 1k output tokens). Prompt pack (zip) includes the starter prompts and the 40-case regression set we discussed. Live links in the email below.

Primary asks / next steps:
1) Confirm target pilot SLOs (latency p95, throughput target, cost cap) so we can finalize instance sizing.
2) Approve test sweep: run Option A + B across your 4 canonical prompt families + our 40-case regression set; allow 48 hrs for runs.
3) Procurement: please share your preferred SOW template & billing contact so we can send a draft (attached: SOW draft v1).
4) Decide on fallback policy: do you want automatic fallback from A->B->C on quality triggers or region/capacity fallback only? We recommend A primary with graceful failover to B; selective C routing for flagged legal/financial queries.

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule the runs and create a canary rollout plan in the Redwood Console.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: zenovia_benchmark_summary.pdf, zenovia_prompt_pack_v1.zip, zenovia_sow_draft_v1.docx
From: Sara Patel <sara@zenovia.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom@zenovia.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Zenovia pilot — recommended model slate & action items

Rishi — thanks, this is super helpful and clear. A couple quick notes from our side after reviewing the deck:  

- Latency target: our product PMs want to keep p95 under 300ms for the pilot (we can tolerate slightly higher for high-risk content).
- Cost cap: we have an initial monthly pilot budget of $8k; curious about your per-1k-token cost estimates for Option A vs B.
- Data retention / compliance: we need to confirm where logs are stored and retention defaults for the pilot — Claire (CTO) asked specifically about audit logs and SOC2 evidence.

Tom and I are aligned with Option A as primary but would like to see the comparative runs for A vs B before committing to fallback logic. Also, for selective C routing: can we do label-based routing from the first-turn classifier? We want to avoid routing everything to C because of cost.

For procurement: procurement@zenovia.ai is the right contact. We’ll take a look at the SOW draft and get back on redlines.

Thanks — can you run the A vs B sweep and share the short report & recommended default?

— Sara
Product Lead, Zenovia AI
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:15:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Zenovia pilot — recommended model slate & action items (client response)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Sara's reply. Highlights: 300ms p95 target, $8k/month pilot budget, procurement contact copied. They want A vs B comparative runs and label-based selective routing for C if needed.

Notes for the run team:
- Run configuration: 50k tokens/sample sweep across the 4 prompt families + 40-case regression. Capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens estimate, hallucination rate (manual label), and embedding drift per session.
- Quick thresholds to flag: if A's hallucination rate > 8% vs B, recommend default B. If p95(A) < 300ms and cost(A) <= 0.6 * cost(B), recommend A.
- Routing plan: implement deterministic label classifier that emits a "high-risk" flag (binary). If flagged then route to B; only route to C when manual review or explicit label set for legal/finance.

I’m putting the allowed run window as 48 hours once infra is green — please prioritize. Marissa, can you own sending the DocuSign SOW once procurement confirms details? Ben, can you own the initial bench runs (infra config + run book)? I’ll draft the canary rollout policy.

Thanks — Rishi
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@zenovia.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom@zenovia.ai>, procurement@zenovia.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T10:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Zenovia pilot — recommended model slate & action items

Hi Sara / Tom — quick update and links below. We kicked off the A vs B comparative runs this morning and have the first tranche of results in the shared Drive. Early takeaways (first 10k tokens):

- Option A (Redwood-mix-7B-quant): p95 ~165ms, hallucination rate ~7.2%, cost est ~ $0.45 / 1k tokens.
- Option B (RedServe-13B-opt): p95 ~245ms, hallucination rate ~4.1%, cost est ~ $1.10 / 1k tokens.
- Differential: A hits your latency SLO easily and stays well under budget if traffic shape remains as discussed; B reduces hallucinations by ~43% but ~2.4x token cost.

Recommendation: Proceed with Option A as the pilot default with a simple label-based escalation to B for any session flagged by the high-risk classifier. Keep C available as an on-call fallback for legal/finance escalations only. This configuration should keep initial spend within the $8k cap while meeting the 300ms p95 target for most traffic.

Attached: trimmed benchmark PDF + prompt pack. Next steps:
- Sara / Procurement: confirm payment terms and SOW redlines so we can provision Dedicated pilot capacity if desired.
- Zenovia: confirm whether you want automatic fallback (A->B) after a single classifier flag or after 2 consecutive flags in a session — we recommend 2 consecutive flags to reduce oscillation.
- Redwood: we will set up a canary rollout (5% traffic) for the first 48 hours, capture metrics and then expand to 100% if stable.

Docs and quick links:
- Benchmark folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ZenoviaBenchmarks
- Prompt pack: attached (zenovia_prompt_pack_v1.zip)
- Eval dashboard (read-only): https://app.redwood.ai/evals/zenovia-quick-eval

If you want, I can schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
